title: Adaptive Soft-Open Fallback Controller for Region/Tier Routing
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design and implement a controller that triggers automatic fallbacks and circuit-breaker state transitions across region and tier routing. The controller must combine multi-signal thresholds (429s, timeouts, error-rate, p99 latency), per-tenant trip scoring with exponential decay, and a soft-open strategy to re-enable traffic gradually to previously degraded variants or regions.
technical_design:
Core concepts:
- Multi-signal scoring: maintain a sliding-window signal vector per route+variant+region containing 429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, and queue depth. Signals are normalized and combined into a composite trip score.
- Per-tenant and per-route decay: trip scores decay with configurable half-life to avoid permanent blacklisting after transient spikes.
- Soft-open mode: when a circuit transitions from open->soft-open, route a small randomized fraction of traffic through the recovering variant with token-budget-aware caps and deterministic jitter to avoid stampedes. Traffic percentage ramps up on successful responses and ramps down on adverse signals.
- Probabilistic fallback: on borderline thresholds, run a probabilistic selection that favors lower-cost/less-loaded compatible variants by weighted sampling rather than immediate full cutover. This reduces oscillation.
- Tier-aware routing: controller accounts for customer tier and SLOs; P0/P1 customers get higher retry budget and stricter failover latency targets.
- Regional grace windows: during rolling maintenance or known region-degraded events, the controller applies a region grace window to prevent immediate circuit trips, using a longer decay and higher hysteresis.
- Circuit states: CLOSED, OPEN, SOFT_OPEN, COOLDOWN. Each state has explicit entry/exit conditions and timers. Soft-open includes success-rate and latency gating.
- Backoff scheduler: exponential backoff with randomized jitter and an adaptive cooldown cap that grows if repeated trips occur within a short timeframe.
Implementation notes:
- Store trip scores and state in our existing global signals store with hot-path caching at the router for latency-sensitive checks.
- Expose a feature-flagged rollout toggle and per-tenant overrides in the Console.
- Provide per-route policy config DSL: thresholds, decay_half_life_seconds, soft_open_initial_rate, ramp_success_threshold, cooldown_base_seconds.
- Integrate with existing fallback variant catalogue and model-compatibility matrix to ensure safe substitutions (e.g., quantized variant with same tokenizer).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can detect 429 spike and move route to OPEN state within configured window
Soft-open mode successfully routes staged traffic and automatically closes if success-rate and latency gates are met
Circuit-breaker state changes and composite trip scores are emitted to telemetry with <5ms local-check overhead
Tiered routing honors per-customer SLO overrides in failover decisions
Probabilistic fallback prevents oscillation in at least 90% of synthetic flapping scenarios in load tests
Console exposes per-route controls and a readout of recent trip-score history and state transitions
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime gating. 2) Unit + integration test coverage in CI. 3) Canary deployment: enable for internal org and 2 low-traffic customers for 48h. 4) Enable probabilistic fallback and soft-open for 10% of routing decisioners globally for 72h. 5) Ramp to 100% with monitoring and rollback playbook. 6) Post-rollout 2-week observation and SLO comparison against baseline.
telemetry: metric: routing.trip_score (tagged by route, variant, region, tenant)
alerts: high open-circuit-rate (>5% routes in OPEN for >15m), soft-open-failure-rate (>10% over 5m)
test_plan: unit tests for trip-score normalization and decay math
integration: inject 429/timeouts to validate state transitions and soft-open ramp logic
load: multi-region chaos tests simulating partial region outage and verifying probabilistic fallback behavior
canary A/B: compare cost-per-success token economics with/without fallback controller enabled
fuzz: randomized signal bursts against ensemble of policies to find oscillation cases

open_questions: What is the default half-life for trip-score decay that balances sensitivity vs. stability? (proposal: 300s)
Should soft-open initial rate be uniform 1% or token-budget-aware by route? (proposal: token-budget-aware)
How should we prioritize variant selection when multiple compatible fallbacks exist? (cost, latency, age, quantization level)
What guardrails to expose to customers for per-tenant overrides to prevent misuse?
